points.description: States that all insertion and deletion operations can be performed in constant time, i.e. O(1), without a traversal whose cost depends on the list length. Equivalent wording such as 'insert/delete in constant time' or 'O(1) insertion and deletion' earns the marks. Saying only that operations are faster/easier/more efficient, or only that the list can be traversed in both directions, does not earn full marks for this point.
points.partial_credit: Half credit for a vague efficiency claim without constant time/O(1).

levels.says: Says insertion/deletion is faster, easier or more efficient, but does not state constant time or O(1).

points.description: States that the constant-time insertion/deletion advantage includes operations before a given location/node in the list or at the end of the list, e.g. deleting a given node or inserting before/after a given node without scanning to its predecessor. Naming either before a given location or at the end earns the point; mentioning only general insertion/deletion without these cases does not.
points.partial_credit: Half credit for naming only one of the two cases, or for saying no predecessor search is needed without tying it to the before/end cases.

levels.says: Mentions only one of the two cases (before a given location or at the end), or says no traversal to the predecessor is needed without naming the before/end cases.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both the constant-time insertion/deletion claim and the specific cases before a given location or at the end of the list. Part marks are available for a vague efficiency claim or for naming only one of the specific cases. A claim only of bidirectional traversal, or only that operations are easier, does not earn full marks.
